decisions.statement: Which paths a page claims is worked out here for whatever files them.
A page states its own path and the file each file property of the page names.
A page claims everything the page states.
A page claims the sops file beside the page only where the page's type declares a secret.
A page claims that sops file only where that file is there.
A page whose type declares an uncommitted value claims the uncommitted file beside the page.
A page claims that uncommitted file only where that file is there.
A page whose type gives a file property a default claims that property's file beside the page.
That property's file is claimed only where that file is there.
That file is claimed from the page's type rather than from the values the page states.
That file is held under the extension its declaration states as a default.
A declaration fixing a file property's value claims that file the same way.
A page states nothing for such a property.
A page whose type declares a file property group claims a file beside the page for each member.
A member's file is claimed only where that file is there.
Each member's file is named by the group's slug and then the member's slug.
A member the group declares uncommitted is claimed under the name an uncommitted file has.
A page of a group's own page type claims no member's file beside that page.
A file property declared uncommitted is claimed under the name an uncommitted file has.
A file property declared with a default alone is claimed under the name a committed file has.
The numbered files of an uncommitted property are claimed as the files of a stated property are.
A property the page states is claimed under its uncommitted name where its type holds it so.
A property whose file is named outright is claimed once rather than twice.
A property a page states and its type defaults is claimed once rather than twice.
The naming grammar lets no other page claim either file.
A page claims a numbered file of a property only where that file is there.
A page claims a file it does not state only where that file is there.
A page claims a file it states whether or not that file is there.
Which properties a page type holds in a file is not answered here.
A page claims a folder beside the page under the name that folder's property states.
A page claims a folder only where the page states that the page has it.
A page claims a folder whether or not that folder is there.
A folder a build writes is told apart here from a folder that is not.
The page claiming a path is answered from that path rather than from an index.
A path the naming grammar reads as a page of a known type is its own page.
A path named for a page is claimed by that page in the same folder.
A path no grammar names is claimed by whichever page type declares that name outright.
Such a name is read against each folder above the path in turn.
The claimant is the page of that type sitting in the folder the name is read against.
A folder holding no page of that type leaves the path claimed by nothing.
A path beneath a folder a page names is claimed by that page however deep the path sits.
A name a page type declares for a file claims nothing beneath that name.
A path closing with an extension a page type declares is claimed by that page beside it.
A page in a folder above the path claims that path through no extension.
A name or folder a page type declares is read before an extension it declares.
Which pages sit in a folder is handed in rather than read here.
A caller judging an answer hands in the pages as that answer leaves them.
The names page types declare are gathered once for a set of types rather than once for each path.
A caller holding a reading asks here for a claimant rather than gathering the answers itself.
The answers a reading gives for claiming are gathered once for that reading.

definition: the paths a page's value claims, and the page a path is claimed by
